A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. All 26 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison of the definitions, proofs, algorithms, and presentation.

before.justification: v1 presents definitions, theoretical constructions, and proofs. The VA3 attack percentages and Shannon entropy estimates are attributed to prior work, not original empirical studies.

after.justification: v2 likewise reports theoretical work without original empirical outcomes. Its added risk-tolerance examples are hypothetical calculations, and Appendix B.3 retains results attributed to VA3.

M1.justification: The key-value construction, sharded-safe, CP, and reconstruction procedures are retained. Trainkv moves from v1 Algorithm 1 to v2 Algorithm 3 with equivalent, more compact pseudocode.

E1.justification: Neither version uses actual training or evaluation datasets. The added novelist and wedding-toast examples illustrate theoretical applicability rather than evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: NAF, CP/CP-k, and differential privacy retain their theoretical comparison roles. No experimentally evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. The new choices of epsilon = 5 and N_D = 200,000 belong to a hypothetical calculation, not an experimental setting.

E4.justification: The formal counterexamples and discussion of the prior VA3 attack are retained. No original ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or empirical case study is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The revised conjectures about achievable beta do not introduce a statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Appendix B.3 retains the attributed VA3 figures: 0.40% to 13.64% and 8.52% to 77.36%. No empirical result entries change; the revised beta values are theoretical illustrations and conjectures.

T1.justification: Definition 6.1 changes its probability bound from ≤ kappa to < kappa, while Definition 7.6 retains ≤ kappa, introducing a boundary inconsistency. The principal theorems and appendix proof arguments remain, including v1 Theorem 7.7 renumbered as v2 Theorem 7.8.

C1.justification: The five central contributions remain: NAF counterexamples, taintedness, blameless and clean-room protection, and DP sufficiency on golden datasets. User-controlled risk and the indemnification proposal already appeared in v1 Sections 8–9.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's Shannon-based beta ≈ 2^-50 speculation with a conjecture of 10^-6 or 10^-9 in Remark 7.7. It adds explicit dataset-size limitations and risk examples, clarifies the normative legal scope, and compares its indemnification proposal with existing service terms.

D1.justification: Section 9.2 adds limited data-curation guidance: checking whether pairs of items share a copyrighted ancestor, using domain expertise, and obtaining works with known dependencies. These are proposed practices; no implemented pipeline or code/data release is reported.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chatterjee and Fromer, Goodyear, and Livni et al. to support liability and credit-attribution positioning, and removes Shannon's entropy reference. Elkins's clean-room work was already cited in a v1 footnote.

P1.justification: v2 expands explanations of auxiliary information and clean-room reasoning, rearranges Section 5, and introduces subdivisions within Sections 7.2 and 9. These are localized revisions; the main section and appendix sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the notation-summary Table 1 and relocates and condenses Trainkv into Appendix B alongside the other algorithms. Typography and text-block layout become denser, while the retained mathematical displays largely preserve their organization.

improvement.justification: Table 1 and clearer legal scope and limitations improve accessibility. However, the added Section 8 example claims beta ≈ 10^-6 suffices for kappa = 0.1 with epsilon = 5 and N_D = 200,000; Theorem 8.2 instead gives a vacuous bound of approximately 29.7 even when delta = 0. This introduces misleading guidance about attainable protection. With the main theory retained, the clarity gains and new consistency problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
